\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Nondeterministic Space: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.NondeterministicSpace}.

\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Nondeterministic Space: Results}

\begin{definition}[Work-tape positions visited along a choice sequence]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.visitedWith}
\statementsource{BGW70}{pdf-b9fb35a232af-p004-b001}
\label{Turing.NDTM.visitedWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
Let a nondeterministic machine have $k$ work tapes, and fix an input, an initial
configuration, a finite Boolean choice sequence $w$, and a work-tape index $i$. The set
of positions visited by tape $i$ consists of its head positions after running the
machine from the initial configuration using each prefix of $w$, including the empty
prefix and the full sequence.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Space used with a choice sequence]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b001
}
\statementsource{BGW70}{pdf-b9fb35a232af-p004-b001}
\label{Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w$ be a finite
sequence of choice bits, and let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input. The space used
by this run is the sum, over the $k$ work tapes, of the numbers of distinct cells
visited on each tape when the machine is run from $c$ using the choices in $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Visited Position for an Empty Run]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.visitedWith_nil}
\label{Turing.NDTM.visitedWith_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $c$ be a
configuration on a fixed input, and choose a work tape $i$. The set of head positions
visited on tape $i$ during the run from $c$ under the empty choice word is the singleton
containing its initial head position.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Visited Positions Under Appended Choices]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.visitedWith_subset_append}
\label{Turing.NDTM.visitedWith_subset_append}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w,w'$ be finite
binary words, let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input, and choose a work tape $i$.
Every head position visited on tape $i$ during the run under $w$ is also visited during
the run under the concatenated choice word $ww'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Space usage after halting]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith_append_of_halt}
\label{Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith_append_of_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith_subset_append}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine, let $c$ be a configuration on a
fixed input, and let $w,w'$ be choice words. If the run from $c$ under $w$ has empty
state, then the space used under the concatenated choice word $ww'$ from $c$ equals the
space used under $w$ from $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space use is choice-independent]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_spaceUsedWith}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_spaceUsedWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine and let $N$ be its associated
nondeterministic machine, whose two choice transitions both equal the transition of $M$.
For every input word, configuration $c$ on that input, and finite choice word $w$, the
total number of work-tape cells visited by $N$ under $w$ from $c$ equals the total
number visited by $M$ from $c$ through step $|w|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space under a fixed choice]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith_eq_fixChoice_spaceUsed}
\label{Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith_eq_fixChoice_spaceUsed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.fixChoice, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_eq_fixChoice_runFrom, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, let $b$ be a choice bit, let
$w$ be a finite choice word, and let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input. Suppose
that, at every time $j<|w|$, whenever the run of the machine that always uses choice $b$
from $c$ is in a state $q$, the two transition functions agree at $q$ for every possible
scanned input and work-tape contents. Then the total number of distinct work-tape cells
visited in the run from $c$ under $w$ equals the space used in the first $|w|$ steps of
the machine that always uses choice $b$.
\end{theorem}
